actual_scope: Determine the fractional Haemers bound H_f(G_Gamma;F) of the star-configuration graphs of PR #7114 for two graphs Gamma of minimum degree 3 without K_4, the wheel W_4 and K_{3,3}, over every field, by exact rational dual certificates of the Shannon-type rank program; derive the consequence j >= k for star configurations containing either graph.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a helper split with a complete invoice. This package instead answers a graph question left open by PR #7114's port-window theory: whether its star-pattern floor, proved at minimum degree 4, survives at minimum degree 3. No helper basis, split, word or invoice is changed.
bottleneck_link: Side result. PR #6933 and PR #7114 show that a fractional block window cannot beat the tensor lift on P104 because every orthogonal 8-set has a star graph of minimum degree at least 5. This package widens the class of star graphs with that floor to every graph containing W_4 or K_{3,3}, so the same exclusion applies to port systems or sub-configurations with degree-3 vertices. It supplies no paid saving and changes no supplier.
stop_rule: Stop at the first exact certificate that meets the Gram upper bound on a minimum-degree-3 graph without K_4. Leave the prism, the cube and the general degree-3 statement open.
evidence: certificates.json holds 86 and 197 rational dual entries for W_4 and K_{3,3}. verify.py (standard library, exact Fraction arithmetic) averages each entry over the automorphisms of Gamma, checks that the combination reduces to f(empty) >= n+1, rebuilds the integer Gram pattern of rank at most n+1, enumerates all graphs on four and five points of minimum degree at least 3 (27 labelled graphs), builds rank-n patterns for cycles of length 3 to 6, and runs 14 rejecting controls. README sections 2 and 3 give the written proofs.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is j >= k forced for every star configuration whose graph Gamma has minimum degree at least 3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would replace the degree-4 hypothesis of PR #7114 Theorem 3' by degree 3 and make the floor a property of the degree alone; K_4, W_4 and K_{3,3} are three confirming cases.
open_questions.first_step: Run the symmetry-reduced program on the cube Q_3 (20 vertices in G_Gamma, 48 automorphisms), which contains none of K_4, W_4, K_{3,3}; then read the W_4 certificate for a per-vertex inequality that generalizes.
open_questions.blocked_by: No hand proof at degree 3; the full program on 20 vertices needs a closed-set or symmetry reduction to stay small.

open_questions.question: Does the prism, the other cubic graph on six points, have H_f(G_Gamma;F) = 7?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With K_{3,3} it would settle every cubic graph on six points and remove the last small exception to the degree-3 conjecture.
open_questions.first_step: Solve the reduced dual exactly on the float support (2,133 orbit variables) with rational or modular linear algebra, or search the optimal dual face for a vertex with small denominators.
open_questions.blocked_by: The floating-point optimum is 7.0 but the rounded dual was rejected by the exact check, so no bound is claimed.

open_questions.question: What is H_f(G_Gamma;F) at minimum degree 2 beyond cycles, for example for K_4 minus an edge and K_{2,3}?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Cycles have value n. A value strictly between n and n+1 would be a star graph where a fractional window beats every integer one.
open_questions.first_step: Certify the local lower bounds 9/2 and 11/2 with the shipped pipeline and compare them with the fractional clique-cover number and with k = 2 block patterns over F_2.
open_questions.blocked_by: The two lower bounds come from a local unshipped run; no upper bound below n+1 was sought.
